decisions.rationale: carrier has distinct_count 16 equal to row_count 16 with null_rate 0.0, so carrier_code alone plausibly identifies one row per carrier.

_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry only capture-tool artifacts (a UUID, a single constant timestamp, and a constant empty JSON object), so all three are dropped.

purpose: This table is a cleaned, small reference lookup of the sixteen airline carriers that flew from New York City airports in 2013, feeding joins against flight-level fact tables keyed by carrier code.
usage: Join downstream flight tables to this table on carrier_code to resolve the full carrier_name for reporting; the table has exactly 16 rows, one per carrier, with no nulls in either column.
limitations: No duplicate rows or null values were found in bronze (duplicate_row_rate 0.0, null_rate 0.0 for both business columns), so no cleanup beyond renaming and dropping Airbyte capture metadata was required; the single-row-per-carrier grain has not been validated against future loads where new carriers could appear.
